terms.meaning: Antarctica, since about 98% of it is under ice; also called the Snow Desert or Cold Desert.
A small shrimp-like sea animal that lives in large groups and feeds the bigger sea animals.
The nest penguins build in rock hollows to breed.
Antarctica, kept only for scientific research by the Antarctic Treaty.

items.name: Location of Antarctica
items.formula: Around the South Pole, mostly inside the Antarctic Circle (66°30' S).
items.example: Cape Horn, 990 km away, is the nearest land.

items.name: Size of Antarctica
items.formula: Fifth largest continent, 14.2 million sq km.
items.example: Bigger than India and China, about one and a half times the USA.

items.name: Ice and height
items.formula: Ice about 2300 m thick; average height about 2300 m, the highest continent.
items.example: About 90% of the world's fresh water is stored here as ice.

items.name: East and West Antarctica
items.formula: The Trans-Antarctic range divides it. East (Greater Antarctica): over half, with the South Pole. West: towards the Pacific, much below sea level.
items.example: The Ross Sea and Weddell Sea cut in at either end.

items.name: Peaks and volcano
items.formula: Vinson Massif (5140 m), in the Ellsworth Mountains, is the highest.
items.example: Mt. Erebus on Ross Island is the most active volcano.

items.name: Plants and light
items.formula: Only mosses, algae and lichens on bare rock.
items.example: Six months of sunshine and six months of darkness.

items.name: Animals of Antarctica
items.formula: Penguins (Adelie, Emperor, Chinstrap), whales, seals and seabirds live in and by the sea.
items.example: Six species of seals; hunting endangers them.

items.name: Early explorers
items.formula: James Clark Ross of Britain found the Ross Sea in 1841.
items.example: Robert Falcon Scott crossed this sea.

items.name: Reaching the South Pole
items.formula: The Norwegian Roald Amundsen reached it in 1911.
items.example: Scott arrived about a month later in 1912 and died on the way back.

items.name: Antarctic Treaty
items.formula: Signed in Washington DC on 1 December 1959 by 12 nations; in force 23 June 1961; covers land south of 60°.
items.example: Science only: no nuclear tests, no land claims, no pollution, no whaling.

items.name: India's first expedition
items.formula: Led by Dr. S. Z. Qasim; left Goa on 6 December 1981 and reached on 9 January 1982 aboard the Polar Circle.
items.example: More than 30 nations have research stations there.

items.name: India's research stations
items.formula: Dakshina Gangotri (built 1983, now a store); Maitri on the Schirmacher Oasis (1988-89), for 26 people.
items.example: Near Maitri is the freshwater lake Priyadarshini; Bharati is for ocean research.

mistakes.text: Dakshina Gangotri was India's first station; Maitri is the second, still in use.
Amundsen reached the South Pole first (1911); Scott came second and died returning.
Antarctica is the highest continent on average, though it is only fifth largest.
